footer.scope: Robot Tuner is for differential-drive robots: two driven wheels, or four-wheel skid steer with the left and right pairs driven together, with wheel encoders and 1 to 5 distance sensors. Mecanum, omni-wheel, car-like (steering) robots and robots without encoders are out of scope.
footer.offline: Runs entirely in your browser, works offline once loaded, no account, no server.
home.title: Home
home.h1: Make your robot drive straight down the middle.
home.lead: Describe your robot, measure it over USB, then tune a PID controller in a simulator that uses the same physics as our research simulator. Watch what every gain does before you try it on the real robot. When the corridor works, test maze-solving algorithms on the same robot.
home.in_1: Differential drive: 2 driven wheels (plus a caster), or 4-wheel skid steer with the left pair and the right pair driven together.
home.in_2: Wheel encoders on the driven wheels.
home.in_3: 1 to 5 distance sensors (VL53L0X, VL53L1X, Sharp IR, HC-SR04, or your own values).
home.f_builder: Draw your robot from the top: body, wheels, caster and where each sensor sits and looks. Save it as one file.
home.f_measure: Connect over USB and let the robot measure itself step by step: encoder ticks, top speed, motor lag, real track width, sensor noise and timing.
home.f_corridor: An endless corridor with the wall errors of a real, hand-built one: tilts, bumps, gaps, width changes. Or draw your own track.
home.f_train: Let the computer search Kp, Ki, Kd and the speed for your robot (grid search, then a genetic algorithm), and export ready C code.
home.f_playground: Move the sliders while the robot drives. Ghost robots show the same start with different gains side by side.
home.f_troubleshoot: "On the real robot it wobbles" → what to try, with a simulation that reproduces it.
home.f_tutorial: PID step by step, with small interactive demos.
home.f_maze: Test wall following, flood fill and DFS mapping in realistic, slightly imperfect mazes.
home.how_1: The physics is the C++ simulator of the Simulation-To-Real-Life project, compiled to WebAssembly: distance sensors with their cone, noise, dropouts and reading age; wheel encoders; the firmware's own wheel-speed PID driving a DC-motor model; wheel slip and per-robot build errors. An automatic test checks that the browser gives exactly the same numbers as the C++ program.
home.how_2: Your robot is stored in this browser only. Use Export in the robot builder to keep a copy or move it to another computer.
builder.intro: Describe your robot as seen from above. The origin is the midpoint between the two driven wheels (the point the robot turns around): +x points forward, +y to the LEFT, angles are counter-clockwise. Everything you change is drawn at once and saved in this browser.
builder.name: Name
builder.drive_4wd: 4-wheel skid steer (left pair and right pair driven together)
builder.front: Front edge ahead of the axle
builder.origin_note: Measure from the axle (the line through both wheel centres) to the front and to the back of the body.
builder.skid_note: A skid-steer robot turns like a 2-wheel robot with a WIDER track: the wheels scrub sideways. The spin test in Measure gives the effective value.
builder.track_eff_note: What the robot really turns with (from the spin test). Starts equal to the wheel spacing; measure it in step 'Spin test'.
builder.sensors_intro: 1 to 5 distance sensors. For centring between two walls you need at least one sensor looking left (angle > 15°) and one looking right (angle < -15°). Drag a sensor on the drawing to move it; Shift + drag rotates it.
builder.step_tau_note: How long a wheel needs to reach 63 % of a new speed (step test). Used by the simple motor model.
builder.timing_note: Loop period = how often the robot decides (set by the sensor rate). Reading age = how old the distance is when it is used. You do not choose these, you measure them; what you choose is the speed.
builder.motor_model_note: The full model runs the firmware's wheel-speed PID on a fitted DC-motor model. If you did not fit a motor model, use the simple lag (it only needs top speed and response time).
builder.file_p: Your robot is one JSON file. Export it to keep it, share it or edit it later; import it on any computer.
builder.hw_p: robot_hardware.txt is the format of the Simulation-To-Real-Life project (tools/gen_hardware.py reads it). Sensor poses are written explicitly.
builder.confirm_new: Replace the current robot? Export it first if you want to keep it.
builder.canvas_hint: Drag: move view · wheel: zoom · drag a sensor: move it · Shift+drag: rotate it
builder.chk_noside: No sensor looks to the side: the robot cannot see the walls it must stay between.
builder.chk_oneside: Sensors look to one side only: use 'follow one wall' mode in the playground (centring needs both sides).
builder.chk_twoside: Left- and right-looking sensors present: centring with PID is possible.
builder.chk_wheels_out: The wheels stick out far beyond the body: they will touch the walls first.
builder.chk_track_eff: Effective track width differs from the wheel spacing by more than 25 %: re-check the spin test.
builder.chk_sensor_out: Sensor #{n} is outside the body outline. Intended?
builder.chk_wheelbase: Axle distance is smaller than the wheel diameter: the wheels would overlap.
builder.chk_range: A side sensor's maximum range is below 15 cm: in a wide corridor it will not see the wall.
builder.source_hint: Where this value comes from: MEASURED (measurement wizard), TYPED (you), DATASHEET or DEFAULT
sensor.note.VL53L0X: Laser time-of-flight, 25° diagonal field of view (18° horizontal), ~33 ms per reading by default.
sensor.note.VL53L1X_short: Laser time-of-flight, 27° diagonal (19° horizontal), short mode: up to 1.3 m, 20 ms budget, 25 ms period. Our robot's sensor.
sensor.note.VL53L1X_long: Laser time-of-flight, long mode: up to 4 m, but at least 33 ms per reading and more sensitive to ambient light.
sensor.note.GP2Y0A21: Analog infrared triangulation. Narrow beam, new value every ~39 ms, noise grows with distance; reads nonsense below 10 cm.
sensor.note.GP2Y0A41: Analog infrared, short range 4-30 cm, ~17 ms per reading.
sensor.note.HC_SR04: Ultrasonic echo, wide beam (~30°). No echo from walls hit at a shallow angle (> ~40° from head-on). Do not trigger faster than every 60 ms.
sensor.f.max_incidence_deg: Max angle to the wall for an echo (0 = any)
